question: None shared. P-117 is Aljalal et al. 2024 (the PDF map points at a different paper; the correct file is downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S1746809423008959-main.pdf, read for this judgement). It classifies amnestic MCI against healthy controls from resting-state EEG. P-91 separates Parkinson's-disease MCI from Parkinson's disease with normal cognition, using diffusion-MRI tract measures plus clinical features. The population class differs (idiopathic Parkinson's disease against amnestic MCI and healthy controls), and so does the channel (EEG against MRI).
metric: As recorded: accuracy (P-117 99.81%) against ROC-AUC (P-91 0.80), a mismatch. P-91 also prints a validation balanced accuracy of 0.79, which could stand in for accuracy. The metric gap is therefore not decisive, and condition 1 fails whatever the metric.

figures.P-117: 99.81% accuracy (ensemble KNN, 11 NSGA-selected channels), aMCI vs HC, 10-fold CV over 3660 EEG segments from 61 participants (29 aMCI, 32 HC). No interval is reported. Wilson with n = 61 subjects: z^2/n = 3.8415/61 = 0.06298; centre = (0.9981 + 0.03149)/1.06298 = 0.9686; half-width = 1.96*sqrt(0.9981*0.0019/61 + 3.8415/(4*61^2))/1.06298 = 0.0314; interval [0.937, 1.000].
figures.P-91: PD-MCI vs PD-NCI SVM on a stratified 30% validation split of 70 IPD patients (about 21: 9 PD-MCI and 12 PD-NCI): AUC 0.80, balanced accuracy 0.79; training AUC 0.82. No interval is reported. Wilson for 0.79 with n = 21: [0.579, 0.912].

matched_figure_check: None exists. P-91 reports no MCI-vs-healthy result outside Parkinson's disease, and P-117 has no Parkinson's population. No figure puts the two papers on the same question.
performance_validity: The Section 3.5 exclusion applies to P-117 on its own source: 99.81% (>= 0.97) from internal 10-fold CV over randomly split segments of only 61 participants, with no external cohort. P-91 (AUC 0.80, balanced accuracy 0.79) is not near ceiling.
reason: The two papers do not address the same clinical question. P-91's MCI is cognitive impairment within idiopathic Parkinson's disease, measured against Parkinson's patients with normal cognition by diffusion MRI. P-117's is amnestic MCI against healthy controls by EEG, so the population class and the channel both differ (condition 1). P-117's 99.81% also meets the near-ceiling exclusion on its own PDF (condition 5). beyond_uncertainty is false because no shared quantity exists; the raw numbers are far apart, but they measure different things.

quotes.quote: With an ensemble KNN classifier, the highest accuracy, 99.81%, is achieved using 11 channels selected by an NSGA-based method.
The combined dataset has 61 people over the age of 55, including 29 amnestic MCI patients and 32 normal cases.

For evaluating the performance of each classifier, we employ 10-fold CV. This method randomly splits the dataset into ten equal subsets, with one subset used for validation (test) and the other nine for training
divided into 3660 segments (1740 segments from MCI cases and 1860 from HC cases)
Methods: Forty IPD with normal cognition (IPD-NCI), thirty IPD-MCI, and thirty healthy controls were included.
The IPD group was separated into training (70%) and validation (30%) dataset with stratified random sampling.
validation dataset: balanced accuracy = 0.79; AUC = 0.80; sensitivity = 0.78; specificity = 0.75
